title: Ambiguous Entity Hypotheses - scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick personal notes about labeling ambiguous entity spans and candidate heuristics. This is very rough — use for discussion with Maya/Ethan before I formalize into the DL playbook (Confluence).

Context / problem statement:
- We keep hitting examples where span boundaries, punctuation, and mixed-case tokens create inter-annotator disagreement (esp. product names + abbreviations + measurements).
- Current guideline (v2) is too strict about full token matches and drops partial word matches; leads to recall loss for downstream NER training.
- Want a lightweight decision tree + a small set of canonical examples to include in the labeling UI help text.

Quick heuristics I'm trying (ranked by preference):
1) Prefer whole-token coverage when the entity is a proper name or formal ID ("AcmeCorp", "Model-X100"). If annotator is unsure, mark "span uncertain" instead of chopping.
2) For abbreviations glued to punctuation ("COVID-19-related", "v2.1-beta"), include the numeric/alpha suffix as part of the entity if the suffix meaningfully disambiguates (example: "v2.1" vs "v2").
3) For measurement units attached directly to numbers ("50kg", "3.5L"), label the number+unit as ENTITY=MEASUREMENT unless unit is purely contextual (e.g., "room 3B" -> ROOM).
4) If overlap occurs between two candidate labels (ORG vs PRODUCT), prefer the narrower, more specific label for short spans (<4 tokens) unless the longer span is the canonical public name.

Concrete examples with suggested labels (for quick copy into the UI examples):
- "Redwood Inference optimization" -> ENTITY: ORG span = "Redwood Inference" (do not include trailing common nouns unless part of official name)
- "ResNet-50 version" -> ENTITY: MODEL span = "ResNet-50"
- "openAI/GPT-4-like" -> ENTITY: MODEL span = "GPT-4" (exclude slashes/prefix if they are repository paths)
- "baselines (BERT-style)" -> ENTITY: MODEL span = "BERT" (exclude trailing descriptive suffix)
- "3.2.1-release" -> ENTITY: VERSION span = "3.2.1"
- "patient #12" -> ENTITY: PATIENT_ID span = "#12" (include symbol if it is used consistently as an ID)

Ambiguity cases to call out to reviewer: (these should become separate moderation flags in the UI)
- Partial token match where upper/lower case changes meaning: "polaris" vs "Polaris" (person vs product?)
- Slug/URL parts: when the domain or slug contains a product name ("acme.com/widgets"), sometimes label product, sometimes not. Proposed: label only if the slug is human-readable and appears in the visible text separate from link metadata.
- Hyphenation + surrounding adjectives: "state-of-the-art Transformer" -> label "Transformer" only unless quoted name is full.

Annotation patterns we should avoid (common mistakes I see):
- Selecting trailing punctuation (",", ".") inside span — UI should auto-trim common terminal punctuation; instruct labelers not to include it.
- Over-including filler words ("the", "a") at start — trim leading determiners unless part of official title ("The Who").
- Labeling parenthetical clarifications as part of core entity ("BERT (base)") — recommended: label "BERT" as MODEL and add attribute "variant=base" if we support multi-label attributes.

Sampling for quick QA set (10 items to seed disagreement analysis):
1) "AcmeCorp v2.0-alpha released" -> expected: ORG=AcmeCorp, VERSION= v2.0-alpha
2) "experiment-42: batch=50kg" -> expected: EXPERIMENT_ID=experiment-42, MEASUREMENT=50kg
3) "see repo: open-source/ResNet-50" -> expected: MODEL=ResNet-50
4) "the polaris team" -> ambiguous (flag)
5) "session ID = abc123-XY" -> ID=abc123-XY
6) "3x3 conv" -> DEVICE or LAYER? -> probably ARCH: 'conv 3x3' (needs mapping)
7) "GPT4all-demo" -> MODEL=GPT4all? or PRODUCT=demo (flag)
8) "room 3B" -> LOCATION=room 3B (include number)
9) "COVID19-vaccine" -> DISEASE/VACCINE? -> ambiguous, prefer VACCINE entity if context mentions immunization
10) "Lead: Dr. O'Neill" -> PERSON=Dr. O'Neill (include honorific)

Open questions / TODO before I make this canonical:
- Do we add an attribute for 'span certainty' (low/medium/high) in the label schema? That would let us train models to weight examples. Pros: retains data instead of discarding. Cons: complicates UI + backend.
- How to represent nested entities in training data? Right now downstream NER expects non-overlapping spans. We can either: a) prioritize one label and drop nested, or b) produce multi-label training instances with nested spans. Need input from modeling team (ping SRE? Research?).
- Sync with Maya on mapping between 'MODEL' vs 'PRODUCT' vs 'RELEASE' — we need a short decision tree for labelers.

Notes to self:
- Add 20 more edge-case samples pulled from recent QA batch (folder: qalogs/sep-2025).
- Draft a short 2-min video walkthrough for labelers showing 5 examples + how to flag.
- Bring this to labeling sync on Wednesday; ask for a volunteer to prototype 'span certainty' toggle in the UI.

Slack refs: #dl-guidelines thread (search: "hyphenation disagreement"), and the PR linked above (labeling-scripts/pull/89) modifies the auto-trimmer rule — check if it will auto-remove '#' from ids (shouldn't).

End of scratchpad. Comments from Ethan/Maya welcome — I'll fold them into a formal doc once we hit consensus.
